style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: Extreme close-up macro photograph, 100mm macro lens, one razor-sharp focal plane. A heavy, worn industrial freight scale tray holding a single, precision-machined aluminum part. Resting right next to the small part on the same tray is a massive, disproportionately large, weathered cast-iron calibration weight. Shallow depth of field, visible surface texture, metallic dust, soft directional daylight. The mismatched objects are off-centre on the thirds, with the background falling away into deep shadow. Muted, sophisticated color palette, editorial restraint, wide framing with generous negative space.
negative_prompt: text, numbers, letters, UI, watermark, logo, people, generic office, abstract shapes, light bulb, scales of justice
rationale: The editorial macro treatment is perfect for focusing on a specific physical mismatch—a precise measurement versus a blunt, oversized one. It isolates the error in calculation by showing tactile, real-world objects used for measurement and buffering.
subject: an industrial freight scale holding a small machined part next to a massive cast-iron weight
alt_text: Industrial scale holding a small aluminum part next to a massive cast-iron weight.
caption: Using the wrong metric to size safety stock creates a massive mismatch between what is needed and what is held.
title: safety-stock-mismatch-scale
